title: D2CS - Documents Graph Clustering using LLM supervision
subcategory: graph-based document clustering with iterative LLM feedback on edge weights
problem: Embedding-based clustering does not guarantee thematic consistency of clusters, and there is no combined evaluation of clustering plus summarisation.
architecture: Each document is a bag of sentence embeddings (KDE filtering of very rare/frequent sentences); energy distance between bags defines a kNN graph clustered with Leiden; an LLM summarises each cluster, a second LLM refines the summary, and LLM-judged 'success rate' scores update edge weights iteratively; optional user-supplied prior edges (e.g. shared authors).
llm_or_encoder: sentence embedding model + pairs of commercial/open LLMs (Cohere, Llama and others; 16 two-LLM combinations tested)

datasets.name: abstracts (keyword-based sets)
datasets.details: 8 sets of 100 abstracts with different keywords

key_results: Purity on Newsgroups 0.44 for D2CS vs 0.06 for hierarchical clustering.
Cluster consistency across LLM combinations: average max Jaccard index 0.81 (range 0.5-1); clustering typically converges after 2 iterations.
strengths: Couples clustering with an LLM-based coherence check and summarisation.
Can absorb prior knowledge as extra graph edges.

limitations.text: LLM biases can propagate to the clustering.
Very large corpora (tens of thousands of texts) remain challenging because of LLM cost and context limits.
No standard benchmark for combined clustering and summarisation, so no benchmark comparison was performed.
Density filtering helps small sets but reduced accuracy on Reuters.

notes: Evaluation relies largely on LLM-judged scores.
